facts.statement: Eretmosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur meaning "oar lizard" that lived during the Early and Middle Jurassic in England and Russia.
facts.quote: Eretmosaurus (meaning "oar lizard") is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Early and Middle Jurassic of England and Russia.

facts.statement: Two species of Eretmosaurus are known: E. rugosus and E. dubius.
facts.quote: Two species are known: E. rugosus and E. dubius.

facts.statement: Richard Owen first described the specimens of E. rugosus in 1840, originally naming them Plesiosaurus rugosus.
facts.quote: Owen (1840) was the first to describe the specimens, which were named as Plesiosaurus rugosus.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley named Eretmosaurus rugosus in 1874 based on the headless skeleton specimen NHMUK 14435.
facts.quote: Seeley used NHMUK 14435 as the basis for naming Eretmosaurus rugosus in 1874.

facts.statement: Brown and Bardet petitioned the ICZN in 1994 regarding the lost holotype, leading to NHMUK 14435 being designated the official neotype in 1996.
facts.quote: a petition was filed with the ICZN over the holotype by Brown and Bardet (1994), and NHMUK 14435 was allocated as the official neotype in 1996.

facts.statement: A fragmentary specimen of E. rugosus was identified from the Middle Jurassic of Siberia by Menner in 1992.
facts.quote: A fragmentary specimen of Eretmosaurus rugosus has also been identified from the Middle Jurassic of Siberia by Menner (1992).

facts.statement: A partial skull and skeleton of E. dubius was discovered in the Harpoceras faleifer zone at Whitby, England, and initially described by Blake and Tate in 1876 as Plesiosaurus dubius.
facts.quote: A partial skull and skeleton belonging to a plesiosaur was discovered in the Harpoceras faleifer zone, Whitby, England and it was initially described by Blake & Tate (1876) as a species of Plesiosaurus known as P. dubius.

facts.statement: The classification of Eretmosaurus has shifted over time, moving from Rhomaleosauridae to Pliosauridae, then Elasmosauridae, and most recently to Microcleididae.
facts.quote: Eretmosaurus was classified into Rhomaleosauridae by Persson (1963), then into Pliosauridae by Brown (1981), then into Elasmosauridae by Bardet (1995) and Bardet et al. (1999), and most recently into Microcleididae by Benson et al. (2012).

facts.statement: Eretmosaurus lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype of E. rugosus consists of vertebrae, girdles, and limb bones discovered in Granby, Nottinghamshire, within the Asteroceras obtusum zone of the Lower Lias Formation.
rejected.quote: The holotype of E. rugosus has no known recorded specimen number and it consists of vertebrae, girdles, and limb bones discovered in Granby, Nottinghamshire where the Asteroceras obtusum zone of the Lower Lias Formation outcrops.
